## Historical audit: S0140

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C1/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to this file. The supplied observations contain complete JSONL lines, not split observations; the ranges identify their full character spans.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1, [0,10107) | The task was to reconstruct an indoor RGB photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching framing, perspective, occlusion and materials. The image itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5, [0,10172), [0,10823), [0,20399) | Step 1 built multiple named assemblies: architecture, island and faucet, extractor, cabinetry and ovens, kettle, posts and partition. Code specified procedural timber color and extractor bump, a camera and area lights. Blender reported `ok: true` and saved a render and scene. |
| Student response/execution, lines 9–11, [0,10066), [0,10718), [0,20275) | The student *diagnosed* insufficient image occupancy, a narrow island end and washed-out dark areas. Step 2 changed lens 39→51 and shift, rotated and deepened the island, rotated the hood and reduced lighting; it rendered successfully. These diagnoses are not independently verified here. |
| Student response/execution, lines 15–17, [0,10307), [0,10957), [0,20277) | The student then diagnosed a narrow, low island, misplaced post, low tower and gray ceiling. Step 3 lengthened and raised the island, moved and narrowed the post, raised the tower and darkened materials and lights. Execution again reported success and a saved render. |
| Review and selection, lines 19–22, [0,103398), [0,4303), [0,349), [0,59) | With no executions remaining, the student received a request containing the third render and chose `SELECT 3`; the final selection event records step 3. |

**Scene and connection check.** Multiple distinct objects and component meshes are evidenced by code, not independently by inspected images. The faucet is included in the island assembly, which is resized and rotated around an explicit pivot; this is an organizational connection, not proof of physical contact. The sink is represented by layered thin boxes, not a demonstrated cut basin. Relative island and hood pose, camera framing, lighting and material appearance were revised, but their match to the photograph remains unverified. Hood-to-ceiling attachment and rear clearance were explicitly uncertain in student comments (lines 3 and 15).

**Teacher input and exploration.** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis or proposed update appears in the supplied trajectory, and no teacher advice or adoption can be established. The runner supplied render feedback and comparison instructions; the student independently proposed and executed two revisions. Session records report zero tool calls within the student CLI sessions (lines 2, 8, 14 and 20).

**Outcome and lessons.** Three builds formally executed and rendered successfully, and step 3 was selected. **Visual or geometric correctness is unknown:** neither reference nor render pixels are available to this audit, and execution success is not a similarity score. A transferable process observation is the separation of camera, object and lighting parameters followed by render-driven revisions. The particular island dimensions, orientations and lighting choices are task-specific hypotheses; whether they improved the match, preserved occlusions or produced plausible physical connections remains unresolved.
